title: Accept near-miss legacy layouts in migrate
lead: `migrate` accepts one exact legacy layout, so a tree that is close but hand-written differently has to be edited by hand before it will import.
findings_note: agents-repo request R8: --index, skip non-slice files, ASCII --, trailing-newline normalisation, column mapping; requester is not migrating
boundary: **Not in this slice:** anything that weakens byte-exact round-tripping of the files migrate accepts; the error-message work (S157).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Request R8 from the squalor-xyz/agents orchestrator (failures listed in the error-message slice). They asked for:

1. An option to name the index file (hardcoded `README.md`, `legacy.py:274`).
2. Skipping files that don't look like slices. Today every `*.md` except `README.md` is parsed (`legacy.py:281-291`), so an index under another name is read as a slice.
3. Accepting ASCII ` -- ` for the em dash in the H1 (`legacy.py:26`).
4. Normalising trailing blank lines before the round-trip comparison (`legacy.py:237-251`).
5. Mapping other index column layouts onto the 6-column header (`legacy.py:23-24`).

The requester is freezing their old tree rather than migrating it, so the owner parked this as `later`. It is recorded so the next user with a near-miss tree finds the analysis already done.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. A `migrate` index option naming `INDEX.md` reads that file and does not parse it as a slice.
2. With the index renamed, a non-slice `.md` in the tree is skipped and reported as an info line, not an error.
3. An H1 of `# S15 -- Title` parses, and the migrated title is `Title`.
4. A slice differing only by trailing blank lines migrates.
5. A 7-column `ID | Title | Size | Status | Findings | Depends on | Tree(s)` table migrates when given a column mapping.
6. The fixture tree still round-trips byte for byte.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Settle each sub-request when the item is picked up. The constraint they share: the round-trip guarantee is what makes migration safe. Every loosening must be a normalisation applied to both sides of the comparison, or one recorded so `emit` reproduces the original bytes, never a silent drop of content. `legacy.py` stays a pure parser. The CLI resolves paths, and migration stays all-or-nothing. Split this into separate slices before starting if it is more than one commit's worth.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check` and `git diff --check`. Also run against a live tree via `SLICER_LEGACY_TREE`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit per sub-change on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.
